purpose: Document the protocol for selection-aware interval coverage that accounts for donor-selection uncertainty, and record the feasibility assessment.

protocol.description: For each synthetic event, re-run the full pipeline: re-screen donors, re-fit weights, compute effect, then construct bootstrap interval. This nests donor selection inside the resampling loop.
protocol.donor_reselection: Full geographic control ranking with distinct-physical-site dedup
protocol.weight_refitting: Full synthetic control weight optimization per repetition
protocol.compute_subset_policy: If full 80-site evaluation is infeasible, use a predeclared random 20-site subset (first 20 by alphabetical site_id within evaluation split). This must be declared before viewing any selection-aware results.
protocol.predeclared_subset_rule: First 20 evaluation target site_ids sorted alphabetically

feasibility_assessment.estimated_compute_per_event: 200 outer × 500 inner × 3 methods × weight optimization = ~300,000 optimization calls per event
feasibility_assessment.rationale: The 200×500 nested resampling with full donor re-screening and weight re-optimization requires computational resources exceeding available capacity before the September 15 submission deadline. Running a subset would still require >12 hours per batch and risks producing unreliable coverage estimates from small samples.
feasibility_assessment.honest_limitation: The conditional block-bootstrap intervals reported in the main results are conditional on fixed pre-event donor weights. They do not account for donor-selection uncertainty. This is documented as Limitation 10 in the manuscript. Selection-aware coverage remains an open technical challenge.

interpretation_boundary: Without selection-aware coverage validation, real-event intervals must not be described as having calibrated 95% coverage. They are conditional diagnostic intervals only.
